A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BuildArena study. Their main text, figures, tables, mathematical definitions, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching content across appendix reordering.

before.justification: v4 reports original construction simulations for eight LLMs across nine task-level combinations, including performance, costs, failure distributions, and construction examples.

after.justification: v5 retains those original results and adds GPT-5 evaluations, workflow and decoding ablations, and simulator-feedback refinement experiments.

M1.justification: The default five-role workflow, geometric library, and agent prompts remain unchanged. Appendix D adds an optional procedure that feeds simulation outcomes into subsequent structural refinement, implementing an outer loop that v4 described as future work.

E1.justification: Both versions use Transport, Support, and Lift at three difficulty levels with the same modules and task requirements. Task prompts match across v4 Appendix F and v5 Appendix H. The added experiments reuse Support Lv.1.

E2.justification: GPT-5 joins the original eight models in the performance and cost comparisons. New Table 4 also evaluates Guidance-Builder and Builder-only comparators against the five-role workflow using Seed-1.6 on Support Lv.1.

E3.justification: The retained benchmark protocols are unchanged. New Appendix D experiments introduce workflow controls, temperature comparisons at 0.0, 0.5, and 1.0 with top-p fixed at 0.7, an invalid-action-rate metric, and multiple refinement rounds on 18 randomly selected failed cases.

E4.justification: v5 substantially expands diagnostic evidence through workflow ablations, decoding sensitivity tests, and a structural feedback-refinement study in Tables 4–6, all using Seed-1.6 on Support Lv.1. v4 contains failure and cost analyses and construction examples, but none of these controlled studies.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 64 construction runs per task-model pair, and Figure 8 already displays mean and standard deviation in v4. The new tables continue reporting averages and sample counts without introducing seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: The original eight models' numerical entries in Tables 2–3 are unchanged. GPT-5 adds substantial new findings, including 95.3% success on Lift Lv.1; the ranking discussion now identifies GPT-5 and Grok-4 as competitive. Tables 4–6 add ablation and refinement outcomes, including progression from 0% to 100% success across the displayed rounds for 18 selected failures.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of construction states, module attributes, poses, and action trajectories match across v4 Appendix E and v5 Appendix F. No new or revised theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction foreground two technical contributions—task design and the geometric library—instead of four, while retaining the framework and workflow elsewhere. The introduction also qualifies the first-benchmark claim by acknowledging concurrent BesiegeField work. The central research objective remains unchanged.

C2.justification: v5 interprets the new controls as supporting the layered workflow and modest decoding sensitivity, and explains feedback refinement's benefits and inference costs. The conclusion replaces v4's missing-outer-loop limitation with a preliminary feedback study requiring broader evaluation; limited module diversity remains a limitation.

D1.justification: v5 newly discloses default temperature 0.5, top-p 0.7, and the GPT-5 snapshot, clarifies identical prompts across tested models, and defines the existing failure categories. These are additional disclosures; retained module specifications, simulation details, agent prompts, and the project-page link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction and Appendix A add a targeted comparison with concurrent BesiegeField, distinguishing its structured machine generation from BuildArena's continuous geometric checking. References also add Humanity's Last Exam and ML-bench and remove Chen et al.'s code-model evaluation paper. The broader related-work organization remains intact.

P1.justification: v5 revises contribution paragraphs, removes duplicated interpretation in Section 3.2.1, integrates the separate model-comparison subsection, and reorganizes appendices around the added experiments and failure definitions. Most method descriptions and the extensive task and workflow prompts remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v5 adds Tables 4–6, expands Tables 2–3, and redraws Figures 6–8 for GPT-5, including rearranged radar and cost panels and wider token-axis ranges. Figure 10 replaces three construction sequences with GPT-5 examples. Figure 2 and Table 1 move into the introduction, and Figure 9 is relocated within the appendix.

improvement.justification: v5 strengthens validation with direct workflow and decoding controls, improves reproducibility disclosures, acknowledges closely related concurrent research, and tests structural feedback that v4 left hypothetical. These gains are bounded: the added controls cover one model and task level, and refinement uses only 18 selected failures with additional inference costs. The evidence supports a limited overall quality improvement.
